cbv25:2.2: having arranged milk-rice in a large bronze bowl presented it to the Fortunate One, saying:
cbv25:4.1: “Then to whom, reverend Gotama, should I give this milk-rice?”
cbv25:5.1: “I certainly do not see, brahmin, in the world with its gods, Māra, and Brahma,
cbv25:5.2: in this generation with its ascetics and brahmins, princes and men,
cbv25:5.3: anyone who, having eaten this milk-rice, could properly digest it,
cbv25:5.4: except a Realised One or a Realised One’s disciple.
cbv25:6.1: Therefore, brahmin, cast away that milk-rice where there is but little grass,
cbv25:6.2: or drop it into water which has no breathing creatures.”
cbv25:7.1: Then the brahmin Kasībhāradvāja dropped that milk-rice into water which had no breathing creatures.
cbv25:8.1: Then that milk-rice being thrown into water
cbv25:8.2: did hiss and sizzle and steam and smoke,
cbv25:9.1: just as a ploughshare heated for a day when thrown into water
cbv25:9.2: hisses and sizzles and steams and smokes,
cbv25:10.1: so that milk-rice being thrown into water
cbv25:10.2: did hiss and sizzle and steam and smoke.
cbv25:11.1: Then the brahmin Kasībhāradvāja, anxious, and horrified,
cbv25:11.3: and after approaching he fell down placing his head at the Fortunate One’s feet,
cbv25:11.4: and said this to the Fortunate One:
cbv25:13.1: Just as, reverend Gotama, one might set upright what has been overturned,
cbv25:13.2: or open up what has been closed, or show a path to one who is lost,
cbv25:13.3: or bear an oil lamp in the darkness so that one who has eyes can see forms,
cbv25:13.4: just so has the Dhamma been made clear by reverend Gotama in more than one way.
cbv25:14.1: I go to the reverend Gotama for refuge,
cbv25:14.2: and to the Dhamma, and to the Saṅgha of monks.
cbv25:15.1: May I receive the going forth in the presence of reverend Gotama,
cbv25:15.2: may I receive the full ordination.”
cbv25:16.2: the going forth in the presence of the Fortunate One, received full ordination.
cbv25:17.1: Then not long after ordination, venerable Bhāradvāja,
cbv25:17.2: while dwelling solitary, secluded, heedful, ardent, and resolute,
cbv25:17.3: after no long time (attained) that good for which young gentlemen
cbv25:17.4: rightly go forth from the house to the houseless life,
cbv25:17.5: that unsurpassed conclusion to the spiritual life,
cbv25:17.6: and dwelt having known, experienced, and attained it himself in this very life.
cbv25:18.3: done is what ought to be done
cbv25:18.4: there is no more of this mundane state - this he knew.
cbv25:19.1: And venerable Bhāradvāja became another of the Worthy Ones.
